2016_089_020216spmtg.paragraph: Agenda for a special meeting of the Troy Board of Education held February 2, 2016 at 5:00 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, carrying a single substantive item: a resolution under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to enter closed session for the mid-year superintendent evaluation and negotiations, after which the meeting would only be adjourned. Attached is the February 2016 update on the Superintendent's 2015-2016 goals across five focus areas, which reports that the District's November millage renewal passed with 73% of the vote.

**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Troy Board of Education, February 2, 2016, 5:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast when school is in session on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Agenda**
1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Closed Session - Consideration: Mid-Year Superintendent Evaluation & Negotiations; 4. Adjournment.

**Item 3.A - Closed Session**
Recommended action is adoption of a resolution that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss mid-year superintendent evaluation and negotiations. The item notes no additional business will take place after the Board goes into closed session other than to officially adjourn. Roll call vote lines are listed for Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood and Edmunds, with blanks for the mover and supporter.

**Superintendent's Goals 2015-2016 - February 2016 Update**
Five focus areas: Operational, Business Services, Communications & Strategic Planning, Employee Services, and Teaching and Learning.

| Focus | Reported update |
| --- | --- |
| Operational | Central Office scorecard tracks weekly building visits, monthly collaborative-decision-making updates, and an annual survey; update refers to the attached WIG Scorecard. |
| Business Services | eFinance training scheduled for Employee Services and Business Services staff; additional modules initiated in the last year (cash receipting, ACA compliance). |
| Business Services (budget) | Schedule of budget events developed for presentation to the Board in June and December; Cash Position Report, General Fund Budget to Actual Report and Treasurer's Report now provided monthly; Board Retreat scheduled for March 17th. |
| Communications & Strategic Planning | November millage renewal passed with 73% of the vote; Facilities Study Team meets every Tuesday evening, formal report to the Board February 16th. |
| Employee Services | Monthly Employee Services/Business Services meetings; ACA reporting module designed and implemented in October, November and December; healthcare audit of over 1,200 employees in November and December 2015. |
| Teaching & Learning | Ambitious learning outcomes with corresponding performance assessments; Content Area Teams and Cultures of Thinking implementation - updates refer to the PowerPoint. |

Other Employee Services items: an alternate master spreadsheet of all District teaching positions independent of eFinance is being developed; the payroll Activity Calendar is complete through February 2016 with the full calendar expected by the end of 2016, built on a 60-day advance window; standardization of benefits tasks and employee leaves is to be in place for the start of the 2016-17 school year; employee directory information has been validated in eFinance, periphery data such as teacher certification areas and expiration dates is being refined; a longevity audit of all TEA members was to be conducted February 1st.

**Attachments**
OneTroy Collective Commitments to Ensuring Learning for All 2015, listing three commitments - deep learning as the fundamental purpose (evidence: Essentials by Unit for Mathematics PreK-5, multi-tier system of support design for each building), building a collaborative culture through high-performing teams (evidence: list of collaborative teams), and a focus on results (evidence: common assessments aligned to Essentials, TSD Balanced Assessment Calendar). A Secondary Principals Collective Commitments 2015-2016 deck sets out mission, vision and values, and a timeline of November 30, 2015 and June 1, 2016 principal deliverables. A Department of Teaching & Learning deck lists CAT facilitators, CAT meetings, Sustainable Leadership Network and Guaranteed and Viable Curriculum slides by level.

**Notice and format.** The Troy Board of Education issued a Board Meeting Agenda for a special meeting on February 2, 2016 at 5:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000. The notice states that items do not have to be taken in the order shown and that items identified within the consent agenda will be acted on at one time unless removed. Readers are directed to www.troy.k12.mi.us; when school is in session, meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and can also be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Agenda.** Four items: (1) Pledge of Allegiance; (2) Public Communication; (3) Closed Session - Consideration: Mid-Year Superintendent Evaluation & Negotiations; (4) Adjournment.

**Item 3.A, Closed Session (dated 02.02.16).** The backup states the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss mid-year superintendent evaluation and negotiations, and that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, with no additional business taking place after that time other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The recommended action is to adopt the resolution: "Be it therefore resolved that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss mid-year superintendent evaluation and negotiations." Blank lines are provided for "Moved by" and "Supported by," and a roll call vote is called for with trustees listed as Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood and Edmunds.

**Superintendent's Goals 2015-2016, February 2016 Update.** The attached presentation organizes the Superintendent's goals into five focus areas: Operational, Business Services, Communications & Strategic Planning, Employee Services, and Teaching and Learning.

*Operational.* The Superintendent will provide leadership so that each central office executive leader maintains purposeful visibility, responsiveness and promotes collaborative decision making. Measures listed are weekly building visits measured via the Central Office scorecard, monthly updates on collaborative decision making identified and measured via the Central Office scorecard, and an annual survey measuring visibility, responsiveness and collaborative decision making. The update refers to the attached WIG Scorecard for building visits and collaborative decision making for Central Office team members.

*Business Services.* The Superintendent will provide leadership to develop a world-class Business Services Department, establishing a formal process integrating day-to-day front end and back end central office tasks involving budgeting, administration of collective bargaining agreements, and payroll/fringe benefits, and establishing best practices and workflow within Central Office to maximize efficiency and accuracy of employee services and business operations. The update reports that training on the eFinance system is scheduled for both Employee Services and Business Services staff, with the goal of learning how best to utilize the software to gain efficiencies in all functions of both departments; additional modules within the software were initiated in the last year, cited as cash receipting and ACA compliance, and diligent implementation of additional modules is expected to assist in improving data integrity.

A second Business Services goal is to create a transparent and efficient process in the development of the 16/17 FY budget, including a structured budget development timeline with stakeholder meetings to educate and gather input, and a process to inform and gather input for the Board to monitor the impact of current and future decision making. The updates report that a schedule of budget events was developed and implemented for presentation to the Board of Education in June and December, with budget events also communicated to administration and union leadership; and that implementation of providing a Cash Position Report, a General Fund Budget to Actual Report, and a Treasurer's Report on a monthly basis to the Board of Education was established. A Board Retreat has been scheduled for March 17th to discuss current and future budget issues.

*Communications & Strategic Planning.* The Superintendent will provide leadership to continue implementation of world-class communications media and community support for strategic District initiatives, with goals of successful passage of the November millage renewal in order to maintain full funding, and identifying and supporting the Facility Review Committee. The update states the District's millage renewal was very successful and passed with 73% of the vote, and that the Facilities Study Team continues to meet every Tuesday evening with a formal report to the Board at the February 16th Board meeting.

*Employee Services.* The Superintendent will provide leadership to develop a world-class Employee Services Department, with the same formal-process goal covering budgeting, administration of collective bargaining agreements, and payroll/fringe benefits. The update lists collaborative integration with Employee Services; monthly meetings currently conducted between the Employee Services and Business Services departments; and successful collaboration during the months of October, November and December on the design and implementation of the ACA reporting module within eFinance to generate novel data and reporting forms within the eFinance database.

A second Employee Services goal covers developing policies, procedures and protocol for basic operational duties, including standardization of handbook and policy manuals for employee payroll and fringe benefit administration, an advanced calendar of payroll activities, and employee directory information. Updates: an alternate data source/master spreadsheet of all District teaching positions independent of eFinance is currently being developed; the Activity Calendar for payroll activities is completed through February 2016 with the complete calendar expected by the end of 2016, developed over the course of the school year using a 60-day advance window; and standardization of employee benefits tasks and employee leaves is ongoing, with new systems and procedures to be in place for the start of the 2016-17 school year.

A third Employee Services goal is a comprehensive all-employee audit of payroll and fringe benefit accounts within the Sungard eFinance database to ensure accurate administration and reporting of employee information and wage/benefit data. Updates: a healthcare audit was completed for all employees, over 1,200, in November and December 2015, with employees audited for healthcare and fringe benefit elections/enrollment; employee directory information was validated in the eFinance database; periphery data such as teacher certification areas and expiration dates is currently being refined in eFinance; and a longevity audit of all TEA members was to be conducted February 1st for accuracy.

*Teaching & Learning.* The Superintendent will provide leadership to improve student performance and further the status of TSD as World Class, with goals to identify ambitious learning outcomes for all students with corresponding performance assessments to measure growth; develop a sustainable teaching and learning network through creation of Content Area Teams (CAT) in K-2 writing, K-12 math, 6-12 ELA, Science and Social Studies; and further implement Cultures of Thinking K-12. Each update directs the reader to the PowerPoint.

**OneTroy Collective Commitments to Ensuring Learning for All 2015.** Commitment 1, Deep Learning as Our Fundamental Purpose: schools will build collective knowledge regarding state standards to clarify what all students must know and be able to do as a result of each unit of instruction (evidence: Essentials by Unit for Mathematics PreK-5), and will provide a system of interventions based on examined evidence guaranteeing each student additional time and support until agreed-upon standards are met, monitored and adjusted using a regular cycle of data analysis (evidence: Multi-Tier System of support design for each building). Commitment 2, Building a Collaborative Culture through High-Performing Teams: schools will work in collaborative teams interdependently to clarify what students must learn, gather and analyze evidence of student learning, identify the most powerful teaching strategies/best practices, and transfer these strategies across team members (evidence: List of Collaborative Teams). Commitment 3, A Focus on Results: schools will analyze data from common assessments to identify students needing additional time and support, discover strengths and weaknesses in individual and collective teaching, and measure team progress (evidence: Common Assessments aligned to Essentials; TSD Balanced Assessment Calendar). The document notes latitude at the school site in how teams are organized - by course, grade level, department, interdisciplinary, vertically, partnered with other schools, or electronically - while stating schools do not have the discretion to allow teachers to work in isolation.

**Secondary Principals Collective Commitments 2015-2016.** States the mission - the purpose of the Troy School District is to ensure learning for all members of the school community; the vision - the Troy School District will be a world-class learning institution; and the values - Deepening Learning, Focusing Direction, and Cultivating a Collaborative Culture. Secondary principal collective commitments are to work with the Building Leadership Team to deeply implement CI Plan Cultures of Thinking objectives and to actively support the Teaching & Learning CAT Process to establish Ambitious Outcomes in 4 core areas and a Sustainable Teacher Leadership Network. Timeline: by November 30, 2015 principals will submit a report of their plan for the year for deep COT implementation and a report of actions to be taken to actively support CAT work at their building and by their assigned subject area, if applicable; by June 1, 2016 principals will submit an evaluation of the COT plan for the year and a report of actions actively supporting CAT work. Possible plan items listed include membership and size of the COT Leader Team, percentage of teachers attempting and regularly utilizing COT routines, summaries of professional development opportunities and building resources supporting the initiative, the Building Leadership Team implementation plan, meetings dedicated to CAT building level collaboration, administrative team participation in CAT meetings, promotion of T&L Department work at staff meetings, and additional supports for building level CAT leaders.

**Department of Teaching & Learning.** Goals are to ensure ambitious outcomes for all students and to create a sustainable leadership network. Slide titles cover CAT Facilitators for Elementary ELA and Elementary Math, Middle School ELA and Math, Middle School Science and Social Studies, High School ELA and Math, and High School Science and Social Studies; CAT Meetings at elementary, middle and high school; Sustainable Leadership Network at each level; and Guaranteed and Viable Curriculum slides for elementary, middle and high school.
